# Claude Code Gotchas

> Known Claude Code configuration patterns (hooks, skills, settings.json) that cause silent failures or hard-to-debug errors.

## Entries

- [Hook matcher only matches tool names, not permission-rule syntax](hook-matcher-tool-names-only.md): Permission-rule syntax in a hook matcher field silently never fires; use matcher for the tool name and the if field for argument filtering, and self-filter in the script because if fires conservatively on opaque substitutions. HIGH.
- [Skill frontmatter key disable-model-invocation uses hyphens, not underscores](disable-model-invocation-key-hyphens.md): disable_model_invocation with underscores is silently ignored and the skill stays auto-invocable; all skill frontmatter keys are hyphenated. HIGH.
- [Line-count budgets on CLAUDE.md are silently gamed by long lines](line-budgets-gamed-by-long-lines.md): a "keep under N lines" rule keeps passing while single appended lines grow to thousands of characters and the file's real token cost compounds; budget by bytes (wc -c) and direct feature detail downward into docs with pointer entries. HIGH.
- [Agent prompt style rules do not govern verbatim code moves](agents-copy-style-violations.md): subagents told "never write X" still emit X when relocating existing text verbatim, the violations travel with the copy; enforce by linting the diff's added lines after agent refactors, not by prompt instruction. MEDIUM.
- [A sandboxed Bash failure imitates a missing system dependency](sandboxed-bash-fakes-missing-dependency.md): A sandboxed command can fail to reach files that are genuinely present, and build tooling reports it as a missing system library with an install hint; the false "cannot build here" conclusion then propagates into plans and hedges every downstream claim. Verify the artifact directly (ls the header, run the probe standalone) before concluding the environment lacks it. HIGH.
- [Worktree-isolated subagents never see your uncommitted work](worktree-agents-miss-uncommitted-work.md): An agent definition with `isolation: worktree` spawns each instance in a fresh worktree branched from a commit, so uncommitted changes are invisible; agents then report confident, self-consistent results about stale content ("already compliant") with no error anywhere. Commit first or use a non-isolating agent type, and open every brief with a `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` + expected-line-count guard. HIGH.
- [Scripted bulk edits: replace(old, new, 1) hits the first occurrence, not the one you meant](blind-string-replace-wrong-occurrence.md): A diagnostic names a line but string replacement finds the first textual match, usually a call site above the declaration, so the fix lands on the wrong line and injects an undefined identifier while the real finding persists. Anchor edits on the line number and assert the line's content before writing. MEDIUM.
- [LL-G index bullet format is not uniform — one regex silently counts zero entries](llg-index-bullet-format-not-uniform.md): kb/ninjaone/llms.txt uses "- HIGH [slug](slug):" plus a "## Entries (N)" header while every other index uses "- [Title](slug): ... SEV.", so grep -c '^- \[' returns 0 for a file with 7 entries and that zero propagates into the master index; count both shapes, guard on zero, append in the file's own format, and edit the master line-anchored. MEDIUM.
- [Cursor .mdc frontmatter keys in .claude/rules invert scoping instead of failing](cursor-frontmatter-keys-ignored.md): `paths:` is the only scoping key Claude Code reads; Cursor's `globs:`/`alwaysApply:` are silently ignored, so `alwaysApply: false` makes the rule load in EVERY session -- 9 of 15 rules in one repo, ~21.7k tokens of always-on context. A `paths:` glob matching zero files is the same failure one layer down. Assert both in CI. HIGH.
- [$CLAUDE_FILE_PATH does not exist, and the empty expansion formats your whole repo](hook-empty-path-formats-repo.md): hook input arrives as JSON on stdin (tool_input.file_path), so the variable expands to "" and `biome/prettier --write ""` walks the entire project instead of no-opping, clobbering parallel sessions; hard-guard on a non-empty path, and note a blocking hook's message must go to stderr or the refusal has no reason attached. HIGH.
- [An @import in CLAUDE.md only works at column 0, and mid-line it is silently just prose](midline-at-import-is-not-an-import.md): the same `@path` token that imports a file on its own line is ordinary prose inside a sentence, so the target never loads and the omission is invisible from inside the session (a 24 KB README referenced as "See @README.md for full project details" had never once loaded); the obvious fix is silent in the other direction, since left-aligning a large target can double always-on context. Check both CLAUDE.md and .claude/CLAUDE.md. MEDIUM.
- [A regex cannot decide whether a Bash hook command is `git commit` -- walk argv](hook-git-commit-filter-needs-argv-walk.md): once the matcher is correctly `"Bash"` it fires on every command, and every regex self-filter is wrong in one of two silent directions -- "flags start with -" misses `git -C /repo commit` (global flags take a separate value token) so the guard stops guarding, while loosening it matches `git log --grep=commit` so a blocking hook refuses reads; the predicate is positional, so walk argv and test the first non-flag token after `git`. HIGH.
- [A blocking hook's stdout is discarded, so the block lands with no reason attached](blocking-hook-stdout-discarded.md): a PreToolUse hook that echoes its refusal on stdout before `exit 2` still blocks, but the reason and any documented opt-out are dropped and the agent sees only "hook error: ... No stderr output", so it cannot self-correct; the `exit 0` advisory path is unaffected, which is why stdout looks like it works. Wrap the message in `{ ...; } >&2`. HIGH.
- [$TOOL_NAME/$TOOL_INPUT do not exist, and a guard clause on them disables the entire hook](hook-env-vars-do-not-exist.md): hook input is JSON on stdin, so the idiomatic opening guard `[ "$TOOL_NAME" != "Bash" ] && exit 0` is `[ "" != "Bash" ]` -- always true -- and the whole gate below it is unreachable while looking identical to a gate that allowed the call; a "HARD GATE" on Graph permission changes passed everything for months. `exit 1` also does not block (PreToolUse/PostToolUse need 2). Assert the refusal path in CI, not just that the hook fires. HIGH.
- [A PreToolUse guard that inspects the command text is satisfied by a command that does nothing](hook-validates-text-not-state.md): a hook runs BEFORE the command, so a gate wanting state the command will create reaches for the command string instead — and `git add CHANGELOG.md` stages nothing when the file is unmodified, so the exemption fires for exactly the commits it exists to stop (two releases shipped with bumped versions and no entries). Diff the file against HEAD, verify the consequence (the changelog names the version being shipped) not just that a file moved, and accept that the edit must be its own step before the commit call. HIGH.
- [A hook's cwd is the session's repo, not the one the command targets](hook-cwd-is-not-the-commit-target-repo.md): `cd /other/repo && git commit` and `git -C /other/repo commit` retarget the command but not the hook, so a gate that shells out to git reads a tree the command never touches -- it refuses a correct commit when the session repo is clean, and silently ALLOWS a bad one whenever the session repo happens to be dirty. Resolve the target from the command with an argv walk, scope every git call with -C, and assert the "clean target, dirty cwd -> still blocks" direction or you fix only the half that was annoying you. HIGH.
- [A shared-template sync unwires repo-specific hooks and leaves their scripts on disk](template-sync-unwires-repo-specific-hooks.md): distributing one .claude/ template REPLACES settings.json rather than merging it, so every hook a repo added on top vanishes from the config while its script stays on disk and tracked -- and an uninvoked hook fails open, producing the same observable nothing as a gate that ran and allowed the call (6 of 13 repos, incl. a permissions gate the repo's own CLAUDE.md called MANDATORY). Grepping .claude/ is a false negative (script headers and READMEs match); diff the SET of wired command basenames old vs new, and assert in CI that every non-underscore hook script is referenced by some config. Do not assume the template is newer -- it reintroduced two already-fixed hook bugs that only the repo's own tests caught. HIGH.
- [A hook's argv walk runs zero times when printf omits the trailing newline](hook-argv-walk-zero-iterations-printf-newline.md): `printf '%s'` emits no trailing newline, so `read` hits EOF on the final (often only) segment and a `while read` argv walk executes its body zero times -- the guard falls through to "no match", returns exit 0, and every command it exists to block is allowed while the hook looks healthy (wired, fires, runs, clean exit, no stderr). Use `printf '%s\n'`, and ship the guard with a matrix asserting BOTH directions: a too-strict guard announces itself in seconds, a too-permissive one never does. HIGH.
- [A concurrent session can move the branch under you, and it reads as lost work](concurrent-session-moves-branch.md): Two sessions on one repo share a working tree and a branch pointer, so the other running `git checkout` reverts your files mid-task — grep finds nothing, `git status` is clean, and the harness shows pre-change content as if confirming it. Nothing is lost; only the checkout moved. The instinct to check your branch back out yanks the tree from the other session. The tell is clean-and-wrong: verify with `git rev-parse HEAD` + `git branch --show-current` + `git reflog`, then take your own `git worktree` (symlink node_modules) rather than reclaiming the shared one. HIGH.
- [A hook never inherits env set on the command it is judging, so a `VAR=1 cmd` opt-out is unreachable](hook-does-not-inherit-command-env.md): the harness spawns the hook as its own process, so `SKIP_CHANGELOG=1 git commit` sets the variable for a shell that does not exist yet and the hook reads it unset -- the documented bypass the refusal message itself names does nothing, the user is refused again identically, and the usual next move is deleting the hook and the check with it. Parse the assignment out of `tool_input.command` at a command position with quoted regions collapsed (so a message mentioning it does not exempt), and pin the block message to the working form in the same test. HIGH.
- [`--permission-prompt-tool` alone never makes the CLI ask, and the flag is hidden from `--help`](permission-prompt-tool-needs-initialize.md): driving `claude -p --input-format stream-json` as a subprocess needs BOTH the (hidden) `--permission-prompt-tool stdio` flag AND the SDK's `initialize` control_request -- either alone and the CLI silently never emits `can_use_tool`, completing successfully while reporting in prose that the command "was blocked, this session is non-interactive". `stdio` is a sentinel, not an MCP tool name; the auto-mode classifier waves `echo` through under every mode so a benign probe falsely proves the flag does nothing; a deny without `message` is dropped and the run hangs; and the real CLI does not exit after `result` while stdin is open, so a drain that terminates against a fixture hangs forever against the vendor. HIGH.
